newsitem.title: USA: Dash above 1.69 aims dollar/mark at new highs.
newsitem.headline: Dash above 1.69 aims dollar/mark at new highs.

text.p: Dollar/mark concluded its week-long corrective phase and is pointing at new highs after dashing above 1.69 on Wednesday, currency chartists said.
"The dollar correction is over and this move will eventually end up being a move to new highs," said Thom Worden, global techincal analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.

"It's looking pretty good," said Pete Grant, senior foreign exchange analyst at MMS International, as the dollar flirted with levels just above 1.69 marks. "I think we're still on track for 1.7215 over the short term."
In the meantime, the dollar is staring at more immediate targets of 1.70 to 1.7048 marks, Grant added.
Key support now lies in the 1.6790 to 1.68 mark area, which offered resistance until the dollar's surge on Wednesday.
"There was a lot of trading between 1.6790 and 1.6690 and as long as we hold above the top end of that zone then we're okay," said Worden.
Dollar/yen's jump above 122 and then a temporary push through 122.40 on Wednesday also encouraged long-term bulls.

But analysts said they want to see the dollar clear 123 yen before claiming the February 14 high of 124.82 is back in play, so they look for the dollar to perform better versus the mark than the yen in the short term.
"I'm looking for a retest of the highs middle or late next week in dollar/mark, but it might be the subsequent week before seeing new highs in dollar/yen," said Grant.
"Dollar/yen is actually the more interesting one to watch at this point in time because it has more of a hill to climb," said Worden.
The yen's firmness against the mark should slow dollar/yen's advance, technicians said.
Mark/yen's drop below 72.50 on Wednesday may have invalidated the base of a large symmetrical triangle pattern containing cross trading since late October, they said.
But analysts said they were not ready to give up on the cross as long as it holds above 72.00 in the near term.

At 1530 EST on Wednesday, mark/yen was near 72.35, off from a session high of 72.79. Dollar/mark was around 1.6900 and dollar/yen near 122.00, up from levels near 1.6745 and 121.23 at the open. ((--Alden Bentley, 212 859 1669))
